text:
Alex: hey @jdoe — I see you opened the ticket about the intermittent deploy failures. can you paste the latest failing job log?

jdoe: pasted below. failures started last night after we switched to a matrix build for different node versions. only some matrix shards fail, not all. error is a 403 when the runner tries to mint an ephemeral SA token.

jdoe: ```
Error: 403 Permission denied
while exchanging OIDC token for service account impersonation
Request ID: req_01F3X2ABC
Cloud IAM: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken: Permission denied for serviceAccount:ci-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

Alex: thanks. two quick Qs: which runner type (github-hosted or self-hosted)? and did you change workflow name or repo settings recently?

jdoe: github-hosted runners. workflow is called `deploy-matrix.yml` now (we renamed from `deploy.yml` to split steps). we also added a minor env var for feature flags. nothing else.

Michael: jumping in — we set up the SA impersonation binding with a conditional that checks `attribute.workflow == "deploy"` to restrict to the deploy workflow. i think the matrix rename might have broken the condition for some shards.

Priya: yep this matches what i saw in infra logs — the OIDC assertion is arriving, GH OIDC provider verifies, but when IAM evaluates the condition it returns false for jobs whose `workflow` attribute is `deploy-matrix` so the binding doesn't match. result: 403 on `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken`.

Alex: that would explain why only some matrix shards fail — maybe some jobs still use an older workflow dispatch or a different name. can you share the IAM binding we currently have?

Michael: pasted below (we apply via terraform):

```hcl
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ci_impersonate" {
  service_account_id = "ci-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  role = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
  members = ["principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/attribute.repository/redwood/repo"]
  condition {
    title = "restrict-to-deploy-workflow"
    expression = "request.attribute.workflow == "deploy""
    description = "only allow GH workflow named 'deploy' to impersonate"
  }
}
```

Priya: the GH OIDC attributes we receive look like: `repository`, `ref`, `actor`, `workflow`. in our logs for a failing job i can see `workflow=deploy-matrix`. so IAM denies.

Sam: security note — we added the condition to limit blast radius, which is good. fix should keep the restriction but widen it correctly. options: update condition to match a prefix (startsWith) or add explicit alternative values for matrix workflows.

Alex: proposed immediate mitigation: add a second IAM binding that allows `deploy-matrix` (or switch to a prefix condition). recommended long-term: use a condition that checks `startsWith(request.attribute.workflow, 'deploy')` or check `request.attribute.workflow =~ "^deploy.*"` so future names don't break.

Michael: ok. can we patch terraform quickly? also worried about least privilege — any impacts?

Priya: minimal. example terraform patch to switch to prefix condition:

```hcl
condition {
  title = "restrict-to-deploy-workflows"
  expression = "startsWith(request.attribute.workflow, 'deploy') && request.attribute.repository == 'redwood/repo'"
  description = "allow deploy* workflows from repo to impersonate"
}
```

Alex: repro steps for others to validate (short):
1) trigger `deploy-matrix.yml` on a test branch
2) check runner OIDC assertion in GH Actions logs (printed by a debug step)
3) run a quick `curl` against metadata exchange (or watch terraform logs) — failing case shows 403; successful case shows 200 and token JSON.

Example failing curl (what we see in runner logs):
```bash
curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OIDC_TOKEN" 
  "https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token:exchange" 
  -d '{"audience":"https://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/providers/github","grantType":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange","subjectTokenType":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt","subjectToken":"'$OIDC_TOKEN'"}'
# => 403 Permission denied (iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken)
```

Alex: and example of success after fix (observed locally after updating condition):
```json
{ "access_token": "ya29.c.K...", "expires_in": 3599, "token_type": "Bearer" }
```

jdoe: can we get a hotfix? our deploys are blocked for some builds.

Michael: i'll open a quick PR to terraform to change the condition to `startsWith(...)`. i'll drop a rollback plan if anything odd shows.

Priya: to be safe i'm going to add a temporary second binding that explicitly allows `deploy-matrix` while the terraform change goes through code review. command to run if urgent:

```bash
# one-off (ops):
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding ci-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \  --member="principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/attribute.repository/redwood/repo" \  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator" \  --condition="expression=request.attribute.workflow=='deploy-matrix',title=allow-deploy-matrix,description=temporary for matrix jobs"
```

Priya: note gcloud condition syntax minimal; TF handles it cleaner. after PR lands we'll remove the temporary binding.

Sam: security ok with prefix match as long as repository check stays strict. add rationale to PR and we can sign off.

Alex: follow-ups:
- Michael: link the terraform PR here when opened
- jdoe: after patch merges, retry failing shard and paste logs
- Priya: remove the temporary binding after verification

deploy-bot: Pipeline #4521 failed on shard node12 — retry scheduled. :arrow_upper_left:

jdoe: thanks everyone, will test once PR merges.

Alex: closing loop: root cause = IAM condition was too strict (workflow name mismatch after rename to deploy-matrix). fix = relax condition to prefix or add explicit allowed names; temp mitigation = add a conditional binding for deploy-matrix. security approved the prefix approach.

Extras / notes to include in thread for next time: 
- When using IAM conditions with OIDC attributes, favor stable identifiers (e.g., `repository` + prefix on `workflow`) rather than brittle exact names.
- Add an automated check in CI that prints OIDC attributes for a dry-run to catch mismatches early.
- If you must change workflow file names, communicate to infra/security to pre-validate conditions.

— end of thread —
